cohort: The study analyzed electronic records of 887,683 women who delivered in public, private, and university hospitals in Turkey.
finding: The overall Cesarean Section rate in Turkey was 51.2% in 2017, with private (70.6%) and university (70.3%) hospitals exhibiting significantly higher rates than public hospitals (39.7%), and Robson Groups 5, 1, 3, 2, 4, and 10 were identified as the main contributors to this high rate.
mod_finding: The study revealed a very high overall Cesarean Section rate of 51.2% in Turkey, with specific Robson groups (e.g., Group 5 with 24.4% contribution) and hospital sectors (private and university) driving the increased prevalence of this mode of birth.
